parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans identity and a repealed (2008) sodomy statute, but the operative exposure is societal-plus-state: a national impunity climate where state police are named among documented aggressors against LGBTQ people, attacks go unreported out of fear of retaliation, courts give 'dismal legal results', and media suppression hides coverage. That is tier-2/3 — state-tolerated targeting within a broader repressive environment, with no working recourse — not a universal-exposure rule (no facility/custody ban, borders not documented as hostile) and not an organised anti-trans campaign. Raw counts lack denominators, so violence magnitude is unknowable; thin data with police complicity and cultural acceptance of anti-LGBTQ violence resolves toward high-risk, not midpoint. Visitor-facing positives: no presentation offence, gender-identity health non-discrimination on paper. But documented police-as-aggressor, fear of reporting, and failed legal remedies sit materially below a 0.45-style institutional-exposure profile, around the 0.35 band.
